# Architecture

This is the authoritative design source for Mayon. It is self-contained — build against this document without needing the refinement conversation history.

## Product summary

A personal, **local-first** learning app built around a **branchable chat graph**:

- Chat with an AI about a topic. When a response is too dense, **highlight a span** and **branch** a new conversation rooted in that excerpt — the child inherits the excerpt plus the full history up to that point.
- Every branch is a node in a **navigable tree** (sidebar tree + breadcrumb path to root) with optional **cross-links** between otherwise separate chats.
- From any chat, generate AI **labs** (hands-on guide + progress checklist) and **quizzes** (mixed MCQ / flashcard / AI-graded short answer). Both are **leaf artifacts** on a chat (they do not branch).
- Personal, single-user. Ships as a browser SPA that connects to a local Mayon server container with Postgres.

## Locked decisions

| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| Form factor | SvelteKit static SPA + required Docker server |
| Framework | SvelteKit, Svelte 5 (runes), SPA via `adapter-static` |
| UI | Tailwind v4 + shadcn-svelte (bits-ui), lucide icons |
| Database | Postgres via server; drizzle-kit schema; pglite for tests |
| AI | Provider-agnostic adapters (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Ollama + OpenAI-compatible gateways: Z.AI/GLM, OpenRouter, Kilo Gateway), streaming |
| Branch context | Excerpt + full history up to the fork point |
| Branch storage | **Reference-based** — child reads ancestor messages up to a fork-point cutoff (no duplication) |
| Transport | Browser streaming `fetch` (IndexedDB keys); server CORS proxy when available |
| Labs/Quizzes | Leaf artifacts generated from a single chat |
| Toolchain | pnpm 10, Node 22 (no bun, no Rust) |

### Key tradeoffs

- **Reference-based branching:** single source of truth, light storage; the accepted cost is that a pre-branch edit in a parent propagates to descendants. If immutability is ever needed, add a content-hash/version column later (no schema break).
- **Server-required:** the app connects to a local Mayon server container for its primary Postgres store. CORS-blocked providers (e.g. Anthropic) stream through the server's CORS proxy; a clear "run the server" message is shown when the server is unreachable.

## System architecture

One codebase. A SvelteKit SPA connects to a local server container that provides Postgres, MCP tooling, LLM proxying, and backup.

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SvelteKit SPA (adapter-static) — Svelte 5 runes           │
│  routes: /chat · /lab · /quiz · /search · /tree · /settings     │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  lib/ai      Provider interface · chat stream                      │
│              generateLab · generateQuiz · gradeShortAnswer          │
│              assembleContext (reference-based walk)                  │
│  lib/agent   Tool loop, registry, capability gating, critic           │
│  lib/chat    kinds · entries · projection · presentation        │
│              tree ops · branch-from-highlight · crosslinks          │
│              expound/source-map · selection resolution                │
│  lib/db      schema · migrations · repositories           │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Postgres (server, primary store)                          │
│  • RemotePgDriver: browser → POST /api/db/query           │
│  • Sandbox SQLite: MCP tools only, not app data           │
│  • LLM CORS proxy · MCP stdio bridge                       │
│  • key in IndexedDB                                        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        StorageDriver interface            ProviderTransport interface
```

One seam makes storage swappable:

- **`StorageDriver`** — same SQL schema and repository code over Postgres via RemotePgDriver (browser → server), pglite (tests), or the server sandbox SQLite (MCP tools).

## UI stack

- **SvelteKit** in SPA/static mode (no SSR) — instant loads.
- **Svelte 5 runes** (`$state` / `$derived`) — minimal re-renders, ideal for streaming.
- **Tailwind v4** + **shadcn-svelte** (on **bits-ui**) — accessible, modern components.
- **lucide-svelte** icons; unified/remark pipeline for markdown (`remark-parse → remark-gfm → remark-math → remark-rehype → rehype-katex → rehype-highlight → rehype-sanitize`); KaTeX for math, highlight.js for code.
- **Expound / source map:** highlight offsets are raw-markdown ("code-space") offsets resolved deterministically against a source map (`src/lib/markdown/sourcemap.ts`, built from mdast positions on the same unified processor as the HTML pipeline) and aligned to the rendered DOM (`src/lib/chat/selection.ts`); underlines wrap via `src/lib/markdown/wrap-range.ts` (no `surroundContents`). Selections touching generated content (math, mermaid, copy-button chrome) disable the menu; stale rows self-heal in memory at render time (no DB write).
- **Streaming render** of assistant tokens; optimistic UI for branching, checklist ticks, and quiz answers.

## Database

Postgres is the primary store. Schema + migrations via **drizzle-kit**; queries through a typed **repository layer** over the `StorageDriver`. IDs are text UUIDs; timestamps are epoch-ms integers.

| parent_id | TEXT → chats.id | nullable; null = root |

Provider configs live here. API keys are **not** stored in `settings` — they live in IndexedDB (the browser `KeyStore`); `settings` holds only non-secret handle fields.

### Reference-based context assembly

A child inherits "excerpt + full history up to the fork point" by **reading** ancestor messages — never copying. `branch_point_message_id` on a node points to a message in its **parent** and defines how many of the parent's own messages the child sees.

```
assembleContext(target):
  parts = []
  # 1) target's own messages: all of them
  parts += messages(target, ord <= inf)
  # 2) walk up; for each ancestor, include its own messages up to the cutoff
  #    recorded on the child that links into it
  node = target.parent
  while node != null:
      cutoff = child_of(node).branch_point_message_id
      parts += messages(node, ord <= ord(cutoff))
      node = node.parent
  return parts sorted by depth asc, then ord asc
```

The fork's **excerpt** is injected as a branching seed (a system note) so the child's first turn is anchored to the highlighted text. Messages created in a parent after a fork (ord > cutoff) never leak into the child. Sidebar tree + breadcrumb derive from `parent_id` / `root_id`; cross-links render as distinct reference edges.

The ancestor-gathering walk is implemented in `src/lib/chat/context.ts` (`assembleContext`). Per-row conversion to provider-visible `ModelMessage[]` is delegated to the pure projection module `src/lib/chat/projection.ts` — see [Context projection](#context-projection).

## Entry kind model

Every timeline event is classified by a single durable `kind` column (`EntryKind` union, `src/lib/chat/kinds.ts`). Lane and all presentation attributes are pure functions of kind — never stored per row.

### Kinds, lanes, and classification

The 10 kinds fall into three lanes derived by `laneOf()`:

- **user** lane: `user_message` — the user's text.
- **external** lane: `assistant_message` — assistant text rendered for the user.
- **internal** lane: `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `approval`, `sampling`, `elicitation`, `choices`, `self_corrected` — not authored by the user; collapsed by default.

Internal kinds subdivide into:
- **decoration** (audit-only, never provider-visible): `reasoning`, `approval`, `sampling`, `elicitation`, `self_corrected`.
- **transient** (provider-visible during the turn, persisted as internal): `tool_call`, `tool_result`.
- **synthetic** (provider-visible pair synthesized at projection time): `choices`.

The `role` column records the authoring side only (`user_message → 'user'`; `assistant_message`, `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `choices`, `self_corrected`, `approval`, `sampling`, `elicitation → 'assistant'`; `tool_result → 'tool'`) and is not used for presentation or projection.

### Per-kind semantics

- **`user_message`** — the user's text. Hidden prompts carry `metadata.hidden = true` (still provider-visible; filtered at timeline assembly). Chip selections from `choices` offers link back via `metadata.choicesEntryId`.
- **`assistant_message`** — assistant text. Legacy rows may carry embedded `metadata.reasoning` rendered as a decoration toggle.
- **`reasoning`** — one entry per agent-loop iteration (`metadata.iteration`, `metadata.model`). Never provider-visible.
- **`tool_call`** + **`tool_result`** — persisted as separate rows, paired at timeline assembly by `toolCallId` into a grouped unit (header + one-line summary + collapsible structured detail, collapsed by default). A `tool_result` whose paired call is a `choices` offer is folded into that offer and never rendered standalone.
- **`approval` / `sampling` / `elicitation`** — permission and elicitation asks. Persisted when shown (`outcome: null`), resolved in place on the same row via `updateOutcome`. Outcomes: approved/declined/undecided (swept on abort), allowed/denied/undecided, accepted/declined/undecided. Never provider-visible.
- **`choices`** — single-entry pacing-gate offers (`metadata.nextUnit`, `metadata.options`, `metadata.progress`). No separate tool-call/tool-result rows are written for new turns. The tapped chip is a linked `user_message`. Provider-visible: projection synthesizes a `tool-call` + `tool-result` pair matching the legacy shape.
- **`self_corrected`** — critic phase record (`metadata.issues`, `metadata.attempts`, `metadata.succeeded`). Written only when a correction ran. Never provider-visible.

### Presentation registry

A single `kind → presentation` mapping in `src/lib/chat/presentation.ts` drives **all** timeline rendering — durable and live. No role-based or column-combination branching exists in any presentation path.

The registry maps each kind (plus grouped tool variants and live variants) to: lane, collapsible, collapsed-by-default, and a renderer name. Renderers live in `src/lib/components/chat/rows/`: `UserMessage`, `AssistantMessage`, `ReasoningEntry`, `ToolActivity`, `AskEntry`, `ChoicesOffer`, `SelfCorrected`. Live streaming items (`live_text`, `live_reasoning`, `live_ask`) resolve to the same renderer as their durable counterpart via a `live` prop — this guarantees visual continuity when a live item is replaced by its durable entry.

Timeline assembly (`src/lib/chat/entries.ts`) converts ordered messages into a `TimelineItem[]` union (`DurableEntry | ToolGroup | LiveEntry`), applying hide rules and tool-call↔tool-result pairing. `MessageList.svelte` dispatches each item to its renderer keyed by kind through the registry.

### Context projection

The pure function `projectEntries(entries): ModelMessage[]` in `src/lib/chat/projection.ts` is the single seam through which stored entries reach any provider. It replaces the former `toCoreMessages`.

Per-kind visibility rules:

| kind | projection |
|---|---|
| `user_message` | `user` text part |
| `assistant_message` | `assistant` text part |
| `tool_call` | `assistant` `tool-call` part (`input: {}` — see quirks below) |
| `tool_result` | `tool` `tool-result` part (`output` from `metadata.detail`) |
| `choices` | synthesized `tool-call` + `tool-result` pair (byte-identical to legacy `present_choices` replay) |
| `reasoning`, `approval`, `sampling`, `elicitation`, `self_corrected` | **excluded** |

Adjacent same-role messages merge their parts (carried over from `toCoreMessages`). Golden test fixtures in `src/lib/chat/golden/` lock this behavior byte-for-byte against pre-rewrite output.

**Captured quirk**: `tool_call` projects with `input: {}` (empty), not `metadata.args`. This reproduces the existing provider replay behavior where `toolArgs` was never populated in the gather step. The equivalence is golden-locked — fixing it would change provider context.

### Search behavior

Message search (`src/lib/db/repositories/search.ts`) filters to `kind IN ('user_message','assistant_message')` at query level. Internal kinds (reasoning, tool summaries, asks, etc.) are no longer searchable. The `search_vec` generated columns are untouched — the kind filter is applied at query time, not at index time. Hidden user prompts (`metadata.hidden = true`) remain searchable.

## Provider / AI layer

- **`Provider` interface:** `chatStream(messages, opts): AsyncIterable<Token>`, plus `generateLab`, `generateQuiz`, `gradeAnswer` (structured output / tool calls).
- **Adapters:** OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama (local) — all configurable in Settings.
- **Transport:** browser streaming `fetch` (keys resolved from IndexedDB). When the server is connected with the `llm-proxy` cap, requests to CORS-blocked providers route through the server's `POST /api/llm/proxy`.
- **Key handling:** IndexedDB under the same origin as the app.
- **Generation helpers** use provider structured-output to produce typed lab/quiz payloads.
- **Grading:** MCQ/flashcard auto-scored; short-answer AI-graded against the stored rubric.

## Labs and quizzes

- Triggered from a chat; input = that **single** chat's assembled messages.
- **Lab** = structured output `{ title, intro, steps[], checklist[] }`; runner renders markdown steps + interactive checklist persisted in `labs`.
- **Quiz** = mixed questions; runner has per-type UX; auto-score + AI grading; attempts and answers persisted with score + feedback view.
- Both are **leaf artifacts** — reachable from their parent chat, no branching.

## Performance posture

Token streaming provides perceived-instant responses. Optimistic UI is used everywhere. Database queries go to Postgres via the server over a local network connection.

## Project structure

```
src/
  lib/
    agent/       tool loop, registry, capability gating, critic, deterministic/generative tools
    ai/          provider interface, adapters, transports, generation + grading
    assets/      static assets
    chat/        kinds, entries, projection, presentation, golden,
                  tree ops, branch-from-highlight, crosslinks, expound, selection
    components/  subdirs: ai/ chat/ diagnostics/ labs/ mcp/ quizzes/ settings/ ui/
                    + top-level shells (AppShell, BootGate, Sidebar, etc.)
    db/          schema, migrations, StorageDriver + adapters, repositories
    dev/         dev-only utilities
    markdown/    render pipeline, source map, wrap-range
    mcp/         MCP client, transport, mount
    services/    platform services
    stores/      Svelte stores
    utils/       shared helpers
  routes/        /chat /lab /quiz /search /tree /settings
server/           Node/TS: stdio MCP bridge, LLM CORS proxy, sandbox DB, backup
packages/shared/  Wire-protocol types shared by web + server
```

## Infrastructure subsystems

The server exposes these capabilities over its `/api/health` advertised `caps`,
which the browser progressively enables via `detectServer()` at boot:

- **MCP tooling** — stdio MCP servers run on the server, bridged to the browser over WebSocket; HTTP MCP servers connect directly. Tools namespaced as `mcp.<serverId>.<toolName>`.
- **Sandbox DB** — isolated SQLite on the server for MCP tools, exposed via `POST /api/sandbox/query` with a Settings inspector. Holds no app data or secrets.
- **Backup/restore** — PG-native `pg_dump -Fc` / `pg_restore` for the app DB (in-place, no server restart); the sandbox has its own snapshot/restore.
- **Search/FTS** — native Postgres `tsvector`/`GIN`/`ts_headline` with `GENERATED ALWAYS AS` columns; noise stripped from Mermaid and math blocks.
- **LLM CORS proxy** — `POST /api/llm/proxy` routes CORS-blocked providers (e.g. Anthropic) through the server when the `llm-proxy` cap is present.

> The phased build history behind these subsystems (acceptance gates P2–P5 and the
> P-pg-2 … P-pg-7 Postgres migration epic) is archived under
> [Development Notes](../developer_notes/index.qmd).

## Future seams (out of scope)

- **Cloud sync:** plug a sync adapter into the `StorageDriver` interface; no app-logic change.
- **Spaced repetition** for flashcards.
- **Runnable lab sandbox** (code execution in-app).

## Non-goals

- Multi-user / accounts / sharing (personal, single-user).
- Server-side hosting of the primary experience (local-first).
- Server-side rendering.
